docs.intro: A quick map of what you can put in a heatmap codeblock. Full types, defaults and copy-pasteable examples live in the README and the example vault — links at the bottom.
docs.modalTip: Recommended: run the **Insert Heatmap Tracker** command (or click the ribbon icon) to create a heatmap through a form with a live preview, and use the pencil button on any heatmap to edit it later — no YAML required.
docs.quickStartNote: Reads the `steps` property from every note in your vault and colors each day by its value. Everything below is optional.
docs.linkExamples: Example vault — one note per parameter

params.entries: The days to draw. Each entry needs a `date`; `intensity`, `value`, `customColor`, `emoji`, `countAs`, `content` and `filePath` are optional.
params.year: Which year to show. Defaults to the current one.
params.heatmapSubtitle: Smaller line under the title, for a description.
params.colorScheme: Colors to use: a `paletteName` from the plugin settings, or your own `customColors` array.
params.intensityConfig: Maps your values onto color steps: `scaleStart`, `scaleEnd`, `defaultIntensity`, `showOutOfRange`, `excludeFalsy`, `aggregation` (`sum` or `average`).
params.layout: `default` for the GitHub-style year grid, `monthly` for one row per month, `month` for a single calendar month, `week` for a single week.
params.separateMonths: Adds a gap between months in the year grid.
params.monthsToShow: Show the current month plus N previous ones. Wins over the options below.
params.daysToShow: Show the last N days from today, in any layout. Wins over `startDate`/`endDate`.
params.basePath: Folder used when a box is clicked and a note has to be found or created.
params.disableFileCreation: Never create a note when an empty box is clicked.
params.insights: Your own summary lines, each with a `name` and a `calculate` function over the year's entries.
params.tags: Only count notes carrying at least one of these tags.
params.filters: Extra frontmatter conditions a note must satisfy: `property`, `operator` (equals / contains / notEmpty), `value`.
